transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Rodrigues (Aurora Head of Platform), Priya Menon (ML Eng), Marco Silva (SRE), Lena Kline (CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Redwood demoed latest bench runs. Notable deltas: p95 down from ~220ms (baseline) to ~130ms; throughput improved from 45 qps to sustained 72 qps in our lab under the target shape. Discussed warmup and KV cache behaviour that led to start-up variance.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for making time, quick roll call then we'll jump into the run results. Devon and I are here from Redwood.
[00:12] Evan: Hey Maya, Evan here. Priya and Marco on my side, and Lena will jump in a bit.
[00:20] Priya: hi all, Priya.
[00:28] Devon: Cool, so agenda is bench numbers, talk about the routing tweak we applied yesterday, then plan the two hour load run. FYI some of the transcripts in the sheet are auto labels so names might be swapped.
[00:40] Maya: quick note - we ran three bench profiles against your baseline: conversational short (prompt 50 tokens), completion medium (200 tokens) and bulk embed-ish traces. For this sync we'll focus on the 200-token completion where we saw the biggest delta.
[00:58] Priya: sounds good, we care about tail latency for interactive flows, and sustained throughput for background batch jobs.
[01:10] Devon: Right. I'll pull up the p95 numbers. In the first run (no routing change) Redwood p95 was roughly 150ms, baseline was 230ms. After we enabled routing by sequence-length and KV prefix caching, p95 fell to 130ms and throughput rose from 45 qps to 72 qps sustained.
[01:34] Marco: can you repeat the throughput numbers? 72 sustained seems high vs our production baseline of 40-50.
[01:40] Devon: yeah 72 sustained in our lab under the same request shape you gave us - that includes continuous batching, kernel-level optimizations, and the cache warm-up between step 4 and 6.
[01:50] Evan: were these runs on shared hosted or on a dedicated slot?
[01:54] Devon: they were on a dedicated pilot instance we spun up for the bench - single GPU profile, nvlink disabled, quantize path set to int8-ish profile. Note that quantization diffs between models can change tokenization time slightly - the thing to watch is KV cache hits.
[02:12] Priya: "int8-ish"? we had trouble with quantize shun earlier, the word "quantize" was flagged in our last review as causing hallucination variance — are you seeing output quality changes?
[02:26] Devon: Good question. We ran the regen quality checks — rouge/bleu-ish evals — no meaningful regressions. The quantization path we used is conservative and mostly affects matrix multiplies, not decoder logits rounding.
[02:40] Lena: From a procurement perspective we're interested in predictable tail and cost delta. Can you map unit-cost to the throughput? baseline vendor charges more for p95 SLAs.
[02:52] Maya: We'll provide a cost-per-1M token delta in the bench CSV. Ballpark: with routing and batching your effective per-token compute cost dropped ~28% vs baseline's conservative infra assumptions. We'll attach exact numbers.
[03:06] Marco: Okay, caveat - our peak traffic shape is spiky, lots of short bursts. How does Redwood handle cold-start latency with very bursty ingress?
[03:16] Devon: Two answers: first auto warmup via KV cache: if you enable prefix caching for the common prompts it eliminates first token overhead for repeated asks. Second, routing policy: keep a small warm pool of standing slots during burst windows, and fallback to a smaller variant model for tail requests to keep latency stable.
[03:32] Evan: That fallback idea - what is the quality delta? if we send 10% of requests to smaller variant, will customers notice?
[03:40] Devon: We recommend a canary of 5-10% for tail routing with a smaller quantized model; quality drop is typically <2% on our task-specific metrics for short completions, but we'll run the same evals on your prompt set and share results.
[03:56] Priya: can you show the raw timeline from last night's run? the CSV had p50/p95/p99 but we want per-minute traces to correlate with our app logs.
[04:06] Maya: yes we'll send the raw logs. note that transcription in the CSV might label some kernels as "kernet" or other typos, that's just auto-parsing.
[04:16] Devon: Also important - we observed a steady-state throughput drop when the KV cache hit ratio fell below ~65%. So pre-warming the cache is critical for your typical repeated prompts.
[04:28] Marco: what was the cache hit ratio in the run where you hit 72 qps?
[04:33] Devon: about 78% after a 10-minute warmup. The initial minutes were lower ~40-50% and that's where the p95 spikes came from.
[04:44] Evan: So the plan is to do a longer 2-hour run with traffic shaped as our spikes and use a temporary dedicated slot?
[04:52] Maya: Correct. If procurement okays it we'll provision a temporary dedicated slot for that window. It helps isolate variance from noisy neighbors.
[04:59] Lena: Procurement wants SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM notes before they sign off.
[05:06] Maya: We can send SOC2 summary and our KMS integration notes - we support both cloud KMS and HSM for private deployments. We'll attach the short form to the follow-up email.
[05:16] Priya: A couple of smaller notes: tokenization differences between baseline model and yours changed token counts in some prompts which affected cost per call. Did you normalize for token counting?
[05:26] Devon: Yes we normalized using the same tokenizer when comparing. But tokenization mismatches remain an edge case for some multi-lingual prompts. We'll flag any prompts where token delta > 10%.
[05:38] Marco: during the run did you hit any throttles or backpressure signals in the runtime?
[05:44] Devon: No hard throttles; we did see transient queue growth when the warm pool size was exactly zero. Increasing a tiny warm pool eliminated that. We'll propose default warm_pool=2 for your deployment shape.
[05:58] Evan: can you expand on the fallback playbook? if model variant fails or latency hits threshold, what's the step sequence?
[06:06] Devon: Sure - we have an automated policy: 1) route to smaller variant for percentage X, 2) if latency persists above threshold route to regional fallback, 3) if regional capacity exhausted fall back to queued best-effort with a client-facing retry hint. We'll send the flowchart.
[06:22] Priya: would love the flowchart. Also the A/B test for quality - can you send eval harness to run on our prompt set?
[06:28] Maya: yes we'll push the harness and a short README.
[06:33] Marco: any security implications of warm pool? e.g., persistent KV cache data between tenants?
[06:40] Devon: No, caches are per-customer and encrypted at rest. For private deployments we can mount customer-managed KMS. We also support strict in-memory-only cache modes if you want zero persistence.
[06:54] Lena: good. On procurement, what's the predictable monthly commit we'd look at for dev->prod?
[07:00] Maya: we can propose a reserved capacity plan after the 2-hour run - we'll size it based on observed peak and required SLO.
[07:08] Evan: ok let's talk logistics - Marco will share traffic traces and sample payloads.
[07:12] Marco: I'll share by tomorrow. I need an email for file drop.
[07:17] Maya: send to maya@redwood.ai and I'll drop it in the bench folder.
[07:21] Priya: one last thing: earlier you mentioned kernel selection; can we get a quick writeup on the quantize profiles you used and the perf tradeoffs?
[07:30] Devon: Sure — short doc with perf numbers and where we saw step changes.
[07:35] Evan: timeline? when can we get the bench CSV + raw logs?
[07:40] Maya: we'll send CSVs and logs by EOD Wednesday 2026-06-17. Devon will follow up with the routing doc by Friday 2026-06-18.
[07:50] Lena: we'll review and decide on the dedicated slot by Friday as well, procurement permitting.
[07:55] Maya: Great. Recap — Redwood sends artifacts, Aurora confirms qps and shares traces, we schedule the 2-hour run next week. Anything else?
[08:04] Priya: nope that's it for me.
[08:06] Marco: all good.
[08:08] Evan: thanks everyone.
[08:10] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with the folder and docs.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker overlap was limited; some technical terms were auto-missed ("kernet" for kernel, "quantize shun" for quantization) — corrected in notes but left verbatim in raw transcript.
